A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same TopoLM study. Corresponding sections, Table 1, Figures 1–14, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model training, language-selectivity and semantic-clustering experiments, benchmark evaluations, and reanalysis of human fMRI data, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original TopoLM experimental results, BLiMP/GLUE/Brain-Score evaluations, fMRI reanalysis, and the appendix ablations and baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Transformer architecture, spatial arrangement, neighborhood-based spatial loss, combined training objective, and simulated fMRI readout. Added figure annotations do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FineWeb-Edu training corpus, language-localization and noun/verb stimuli, human brain datasets, and BLiMP, GLUE, and Brain-Score evaluations. Appendix test scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: The non-topographic control and Topoformer-BERT remain in the same corresponding comparisons, including Figures 13–14. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Training settings, functional-localization procedures, significance thresholds, fMRI smoothing, benchmark evaluation, and clustering metrics are unchanged. The new layer-order annotation in Figure 2 identifies an existing display rather than revising the evaluation.

E4.justification: Both versions retain analyses of readout sampling, stimulus presentation with or without articles/infinitive markers, unpermuted spatial positions, and significant-unit clustering in Figures 10–14. Caption and legend edits add no analysis.

E5.justification: Figures 5–6 retain bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals based on ten cross-validation folds and the same statistical-test reporting. FDR correction and significance annotations are unchanged; no additional run or seed information appears.

E6.justification: Reported values and plotted findings are retained. Table 1 still gives TopoLM scores of 0.71/0.68/0.78 and non-topographic scores of 0.76/0.65/0.80 for BLiMP/GLUE/Brain-Score. Revised figures display the same clustering maps and benchmark results.

T1.justification: The spatial-loss equations, Moran's I definition and neighborhood construction in Appendix A, and Islands Moran's I procedure in Figure 14 are unchanged. No mathematical argument or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about brain-like language organization emerging from spatial smoothness and its relationship to task performance and brain alignment.

C2.justification: Interpretations of Topoformer-BERT, the proposed regularization explanation for GLUE performance, and limitations concerning separate layer maps and tissue perturbations are unchanged. Added color explanations do not introduce scientific interpretations.

D1.justification: Implementation, hyperparameters, hardware, training duration, processing descriptions, and code/data access information remain unchanged. New figure labels clarify existing panels without adding implementation or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged, including positioning TopoLM within TDANN models and distinguishing spatial smoothness from Topoformer's local-connectivity approach.

P1.justification: Several captions receive localized clarifications, including yellow language-selective clusters and red/blue verb–noun mappings in Figures 2, 3, 7, 8, 10, and 12. The main narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds cluster-color legends across several figures, labels Figure 2's MLP layers and their ordering, and adjusts panel spacing and sizes, including enlarging Figures 9–10. These are limited display refinements; the figure inventory and table structure are retained.

improvement.justification: Explicit cluster-color legends, Figure 2's layer-order annotation, and enlarged appendix panels make existing evidence easier to interpret. The methods, results, and substantive discussion remain unchanged, so the supported overall improvement is limited to presentation clarity.
